# Exact obstruction to a profile-and-floor replacement for the cap-band barrier

This is a certificate in positive normalized RAW cap/section data. It is not
asserted to have a convex-body realization. It rejects only a scalar step
that discards the actual geometry of an initial triangle and its truncation.

Set k=1 and

    f=(1/25,41/25,29/25),
    r=(16/25,29/40,3927/5800),
    Q_i=q_i=r_i^2,
    sigma_i=2r_i/f_i.

All quantities are positive. Directly,

    sum_i f_i r_i=2,

so M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i=1 and these sigma_i reproduce exactly the displayed
f_i=2sqrt(k Q_i)/(sigma_i M). Thus the normalization is consistent, not a
freely specified f-vector unrelated to its cap data.

The three cap fractions are

    q=(256/625,841/1600,15421329/33640000).

Their minimum is q_1, which exceeds 20/49 by 44/30625. Their maximum is q_2.
The full sorted cap profile obeys

    sum_i q_i-(3/4)max_i q_i
       =134483117/134560000<1,

with positive gap 76883/134560000. The three Lorentz rows are exactly

    (Phi_1,Phi_2,Phi_3)=(2,2,1166/625),

so all are at most 2.

Now decrease k and Q_2 by the same infinitesimal positive amount, keeping
all other cap areas and all three sections fixed. This is the RAW direction
corresponding to loss in unique sector 2. At the tight row Phi_1, put

    z=7/5,      C=99/25.

The exact derivative coefficient is

    2k alpha_2
      =C+z f_2/r_2^2-C f_2/r_2
      =-66193/105125<0.

The tight first row therefore increases in this loss direction. Consequently
the cap floor q_i>=20/49, the full sorted profile, all three row inequalities,
and the exact normalization do NOT by themselves imply the inward loss
derivative needed to remove the initial-ceiling premise.

All conclusions are finite rational identities. No numerical optimization
or hypothetical geometric realization is used. The actual triangle heights,
its maximum available corner loss, and the shared ray constraints may still
exclude these data. They are not discarded in any claimed geometric theorem.
